subject: Post-call: OrionAI budget bands & latency tradeoffs — next steps
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex@orionai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 08 Jan 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: OrionAI budget bands & latency tradeoffs — next steps

Alex — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned:

- Ask: confirm target cost target and token volume ranges so we can propose tiered options. You mentioned a target of "$700–900 / 1M tokens" for production, with an initial pilot tolerance up to ~$1,200 / 1M.
- Volume guidance: per our call, expected steady-state is ~12–18M tokens/month with seasonal spikes to ~40M/month. You’ll confirm by EOD Monday and share the volume file.
- Latency SLO: you want 95th pct <= 350ms for core chat flows. You said some non-critical batch jobs can tolerate 2–5s.
- Tradeoffs we proposed (high-level):
  * Streaming + smaller model variant for p95-sensitive flows — higher per-token cost but lower p95.
  * Batch/async for heavy document processing — much lower unit cost when we can amortize token work.
  * Dedicated pool for production (predictable latency) vs hosted with fallback to smaller cheaper variants.

Attachments: I’ve attached the volume template (orion_volume_estimates.xlsx) and our pricing playbook excerpt (redwood-pricing-playbook.pdf) to help illustrate unit economics across tiers.

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm volumes + budget range (EOD Mon).
2) We (Ben + Marissa) will map 3 recommended configurations: a conservative production SLO configuration, a cost-optimized configuration, and a hybrid canary plan. Expect that in 48 hours after we get volumes.
3) If budget and SLO align, we’ll scope a 2-week pilot: telemetry + cost measurement at token scale ~5–10M.

If you prefer, I can loop in our procurement contact next to align on PO/timelines.

Thanks — Priya

-- 
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
pri...@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Alex Nguyen <alex@orionai.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <pri...@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@orionai.com>
Date: Fri, 08 Jan 2027 16:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: OrionAI budget bands & latency tradeoffs — next steps

Thanks Priya — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Budget target: our execs gave a hard target of $800 / 1M tokens for production; pilot can go up to $1,100 / 1M. If we can demonstrate 10–15% improvement after optimizations, they'll consider moving to $750.
2) Volumes: I filled out the attached sample (see orion_volume_estimates.xlsx) — steady 14M/mo, peaks 38M/mo, expected growth 20% q/q.
3) Latency nuance: the 350ms p95 is for agent UI (interactive chat). We can accept 600–800ms for heavy embedding + rerank calls that are behind a progress indicator. Batch jobs (document ingestion) are not time-sensitive.

A couple asks: can Redwood show example unit-cost math for the three configs you mentioned (costs at 14M and at 38M) including assumptions for batching and expected throughput? Also please include fallbacks in the plan — e.g., if dedicated capacity is delayed, what does partial hosted + quantized model look like?

Procurement: looping them in — we’ll need a preliminary T&Cs checklist and an estimated PO.

— Alex

On attachments: I attached our filled volume sheet. Also note we use EU data residency for some customers; we can scope that later.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex@orionai.com>, Priya Natarajan <pri...@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 09 Jan 2027 08:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: OrionAI budget bands & latency tradeoffs — next steps

Alex — thanks for the numbers and for attaching the volume file. Priya, Ben and I synced this morning. High level plan and assumptions below (we’ll send a formal config doc within 48 hours):

Summary assumptions we’ll price against:
- Baseline model: Llama-3-like 13B variant (quantized) for cost-optimized; Llama-3-like 70B (fp16) for SLO-critical flows.
- Pilot size: 5M tokens/day (~150M tokens over 30 days) to collect stable metrics — but we’ll size telemetry to shorter windows if you prefer.
- Batch savings: expect 3–4x lower $/1M tokens for workflows that can batch to ≥2s latency.
- Streaming overhead: ~20–35% extra unit cost vs equivalent batch model due to per-request fixed overhead + less batching opportunity.

Initial configuration options we’ll price (short labels):
1) "SLO-first" — dedicated pool, priority routing, mixed model routing (70B for chat, 13B for background), target ~$900–1,050 / 1M at 14M/mo.
2) "Cost-first" — hosted + aggressive batching for background + quantized 13B for everything else, target ~$650–800 / 1M at 14M/mo (better at 38M due to batch efficiency).
3) "Hybrid canary" — start hosted for pilot with circuit-breaker to dedicated on rollout; we’ll instrument per-route SLOs and cost telemetry to switch traffic. Expected ~$750–920 / 1M initially.

Ben will follow up with concrete latency vs cost delta table and example token math for both 14M and 38M scenarios. We’ll also outline fallback if dedicated capacity is delayed (hosted + quantized variants + pre-warming KV caches).

Next steps we’ll deliver:
- Ben: latency vs $/1M delta table + recommended batching thresholds (by flow) + suggested model variants (in 24–36 hrs).
- Priya: commercial outline and PO checklist (in 48 hrs).

Marissa

Head of Solutions | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex@orionai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <pri...@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 09 Jan 2027 09:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: OrionAI budget bands & latency tradeoffs — next steps

Alex — short technical note and the numbers Marissa promised. Quick table (high level):

Assumptions: token mix 25% prompt / 75% completion, avg call 280 tokens, streaming adds 0.28s overhead on average for per-request setup, batching amortizes fixed kernel launch cost.

Scenarios (14M/mo):
- SLO-first (dedicated): p95 chat ~320ms, est $950 / 1M tokens.
- Cost-first (hosted, batch-heavy): p95 chat ~620ms (streaming disabled for chat), est $720 / 1M tokens.
- Hybrid: canary 10% traffic to dedicated -> p95 chat ~360ms, est $810 / 1M tokens.

At peak (38M/mo) batching efficiency improves cost-first to ~$600 / 1M and hybrid to ~$745 / 1M; dedicated remains ~ $920–980 / 1M depending on reserved commit.

Recommended batching strategy by flow:
- Interactive chat (p95 target <=350ms): streaming enabled, use 70B fp16 on dedicated or hosted with priority buckets; set max batch window 30ms to avoid tail latency.
- Rerank/embedding flows (p95 target ~600–800ms): allow 500–1500ms batch windows; use quantized 13B variant to cut cost.
- Ingestion/document processing: full async batch (2–5s) — enable large batch sizes and chunk-level prefix caching for cost reduction.

Fallback options if dedicated delayed:
- Host + quantized 70B variant for chat with pre-warmed KV caches and autoscaled warm pools. Expect ~10–20% perf hit but still within acceptable p95 if we tune batch windows.

Attachment: small CSV-style excerpt embedded below for your finance/PO team to run quick math. If useful we can convert to a one-pager.

[Attachment stub: rdw_delta_table.csv]

Happy to jump on a short call with procurement if they have specific timeline/PO requirements.
